newsitem.title: CHINA: HK STOCKS EXPECTED TO RECOVER, BUT GAINS LIMITED.
newsitem.headline: HK STOCKS EXPECTED TO RECOVER, BUT GAINS LIMITED.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are likely to recover on Tuesday from Monday's sharply lower close, after an overnight rebound on Wall Street as interest rate worries eased, brokers said.

"The market should recover on a better Wall Street but gains are likely to be capped as sentiment is affected by banks which raised mortgage rates," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
The Dow industrials rose 30.89 points to close at 8,062.11.
Standard Chartered Bank raised mortgage rates by 50 basis points shortly after Hongkong Bank's 25 basis points increase.
"The rises will have a psychological impact since the market has risen so much lately," Chia said.
The higher close on Monday of Hong Kong stocks in London would also lift buying interest, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index tumbled 187.07 points, or 1.12 percent to close Monday at 16,460.47 but the Hang Seng London Reference Index later added 102.46 points, to 16,562.93.
HSBC, which closed HK$5.15 higher at HK$275.15 in London on Monday, should led the rise today, a broker with a local house said. -- Alison Leung (852) 2843 6369
